subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for FinSecure: Dedicated vs Private VPC (or on-prem).

Summary of what I heard as your top priorities:
- Data isolation: customer data must never leave your VPC or on-prem environment; no Redwood-managed persistence of PII/raw documents.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS/HSM for any encryption at rest.
- Audit & compliance: full request-level audit logs, exportable for 7 years (per your policy).
- Network controls: VPC peering or PrivateLink, IP allowlist, and no public internet egress for inference traffic.
- Timeline: procurement wants a proposal and rough schedule this week to review with security and procurement.

What this means (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to ship but cannot meet the data isolation constraints you described. We don’t recommend for this use case.
- Dedicated capacity: provides isolated GPU pools (no noisy neighbors) and stronger tenancy guarantees. However, in our hosted Dedicated offering the Redwood control plane still handles scheduling and metadata and some telemetry will traverse Redwood-managed services — that does not satisfy the “no Redwood-managed persistence / no egress” requirement unless combined with tighter networking (and still won't give you customer-managed KMS).
- Private VPC / on-prem: designed for these requirements — control plane and/or inference nodes run inside your VPC (or on-prem) under your networking and key management. This is the only mode that fully satisfies “customer-only data residency” and customer-managed KMS.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the must-haves (above) and whether the requirement is hard-block for production?
2) Schedule a 30-min technical call with your infra/security and our privacy engineering lead (Mateo) to walk the checklist and architecture options. I’m including a short checklist and a draft SOW we commonly use for Private VPC engagements.
3) If Private VPC is required, we’ll follow with a rough cost & timeline estimate (lead time typically 6–10 weeks depending on cloud provider and networking approvals).

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (summary), redwood-private-vpc-sow-draft.pdf (sample).

Availability: I’m free Wed/Thu afternoon PST and can send a Calendly link.

Thanks — let me know if I missed anything.

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Confirming the requirements are hard-blocks for production. A couple clarifying q's: 

- By "no Redwood-managed persistence" we mean not only documents but any derived embeddings, KV cache, or logs. All of that must stay inside our control plane/network.
- Customer-managed KMS is required; we cannot have keys stored or managed by a third party.
- Audit logs must include per-request input/output (redacted if needed) and be exportable to our SIEM.

We are leaning toward Private VPC (or on-prem) but would like to understand where Dedicated could meet some of our needs vs where it falls short. Can you send: 
1) A short one-pager that lists which specific controls are available in Dedicated vs Private VPC (networking, KMS, persistence, logging).
2) A rough ballpark on monthly cost + one-time setup for Private VPC (even a range is fine).
3) Any references or similar customers who ran in Private VPC for regulated data.

Attaching our internal security requirements spreadsheet for reference (FinSecure_security_requirements.xlsx).

On Wed/Thu afternoons works for us — Priya and I can do Thu 6/24 11:00-11:30am PT if that works for your team.

Thanks,

Alex — great questions. Below is a concise mapping (Dedicated vs Private VPC) and what we can commit to: 

Dedicated Capacity (Redwood-hosted, reserved GPUs):
- Tenancy: isolated GPU pools dedicated to your account (no noisy neighbors).
- Persistence: inference state (KV cache, embeddings) is stored in Redwood-managed storage by default. We can configure TTLs and avoid long-term storage, but we cannot support full "never persist in Redwood-managed storage" for production in the hosted Dedicated offering today.
- KMS: Redwood manages encryption keys for the hosted control plane; we can encrypt at rest but not with customer-managed KMS unless you purchase Private VPC.
- Networking: IP allowlist, egress controls, and restricted endpoints available, but control plane connections still traverse Redwood-managed services.
- Logging: detailed telemetry and request tracing available; logs are stored in Redwood systems but can be exported via secure transfer to your SIEM.

Private VPC / On-prem (what satisfies your hard-blocks):
- Tenancy & persistence: inference nodes and optionally the control plane run inside your VPC or on-prem. No Redwood-managed persistence of customer data unless explicitly enabled.
- KMS: supports customer-managed KMS/HSM (BYOK) and integration with your key rotation policies.
- Networking: VPC peering / PrivateLink or direct connect; no public internet egress required.
- Logging: full request-level audit logs available within your environment and exportable to your SIEM.
- Compliance: we provide artifacts (SOC2, ISO summaries) and help with evidence collection; our SRE/security team runs a short architecture review during onboarding.

Rough ballpark (very high level):
- Private VPC: one-time setup & integration: $40k–$120k (depends on provider, network setup, and SSO/KMS integration).
- Monthly baseline: $20k–$60k for reserved capacity to support inference throughput (scales with GPUs and replication).

References: we can share two anonymized customers who ran regulated workloads in Private VPC — I’ll loop in customer success for a case study once we have NDAs in place.

Next steps:
- Mateo (copied) is our security/solutions lead and will join the technical call to walk your security checklist in detail.
- Confirm Thu 6/24 11:00am PT and we’ll send a calendar invite + tech agenda.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-sow-draft.pdf

—Marissa
